title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - Food & Agriculture
description: Curated OT/ICS cybersecurity advisories, incidents and threat intelligence from primary sources. Editorial summaries by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

_otthreatfeed.usage: Free to reuse with attribution. Credit 'Mike Holcomb & UtilSec' and link back to otthreatfeed.com and to each item's linked primary source. Summaries are editorial paraphrase - verify against the primary source before acting.

items.title: Fairlife restarts dairy production after ransomware halt — Coca-Cola confirms data was stolen
items.content_text: Coca-Cola’s Fairlife dairy has resumed the majority of production at its four US plants, closing a roughly ten-day shutdown that began with a 16 July ransomware attack — one of the year’s most consequential food and beverage incidents. In a 27 July update, Coca-Cola said it had restored most operations and confirmed that attackers stole data during the intrusion; the Anubis ransomware group claimed responsibility and listed the company on its leak site. Production-related systems were among those hit, forcing a precautionary halt across US plants while Canadian operations continued and retail supply held up on existing inventory. For food and ag operators the JBS lesson repeats: perishable, just-in-time output turns an IT intrusion into spoiled inventory and missed deliveries within hours. Whether ransomware crossed into OT or the stoppage was precautionary, the operational result was the same.

_otthreatfeed.date_note: Disclosed 16 Jul 2026 — updated 27 Jul: production resumed, data theft confirmed

items.title: Cyberattack on Japanese food supplier Nichirei disrupts deliveries, including to KFC Japan
items.content_text: Nichirei, a major Japanese frozen- and processed-food company and logistics provider, disclosed a cyberattack that knocked out ordering and distribution systems and interrupted supplies to restaurant customers including KFC Japan. The company said it was bringing systems back online and would resume operations sequentially from 17 July, working through manual and backup processes in the interim. Nichirei has not detailed the intrusion method or confirmed ransomware, and reporting notes other Japanese food and beverage names — Asahi Group and Ezaki Glico among them — have been hit in recent months. For food and ag operators it is another reminder that an IT-side outage at a distributor or processor cascades straight into missed, time-critical deliveries.

items.title: Iran-affiliated actors are disabling the PLC alarm and shutdown logic that guards food-safety interlocks
items.content_text: The updated federal advisory AA26-097A (22 July) confirms Iran-affiliated actors reaching internet-exposed PLCs — Rockwell, Siemens and Schneider — extracting project files and modifying or deleting control logic, and in some cases disabling shutdown and alarm functions so equipment can enter unsafe states without alerting operators. In food and beverage processing, that same class of controller enforces cook/pasteurization temperatures, CIP cycles and refrigeration interlocks. Defeated alarm logic is not just downtime — it is a food-safety exposure, which is why controller integrity belongs on the HACCP-adjacent risk list.

items.title: Ransomware on food & beverage keeps escalating — 220 tracked attacks in 2026 across 46 groups
items.content_text: A 3 August round-up pulls the year’s food-sector ransomware picture together: roughly 220 attacks tracked so far in 2026 across 46 distinct groups, on pace to exceed the 265 counted for all of 2025, with Qilin, Akira and CL0P among the most active and CL0P over-indexing on food and agriculture. The reporting strings together a run of high-profile hits — Coca-Cola’s Fairlife, Heineken, Campbell Soup, Dole, Krispy Kreme, Whole Foods distributor UNFI and Chick-fil-A — and Food and Ag-ISAC’s Jonathan Braley reiterates why the sector is a reliable pressure point: just-in-time, perishable supply chains feel a ransomware outage almost immediately. Most intrusions remain opportunistic — exposed systems, broker-bought access and phishing — not sector-specific targeting.

items.title: FortiSandbox RCE flaws added to CISA KEV — exploited appliances on the plant IT/OT boundary
items.content_text: CISA added two critical Fortinet flaws, CVE-2026-39808 and CVE-2026-25089 (both CVSS 9.1), to the KEV catalog on 16 July after in-the-wild exploitation. They are OS command-injection bugs in FortiSandbox / Cloud / PaaS allowing unauthenticated command execution via crafted HTTP requests. In food and beverage plants, Fortinet appliances often guard the line between enterprise IT and processing OT; a compromised inspection appliance is a foothold and a blind spot. CISA set a 19 July federal remediation deadline.

_otthreatfeed.date_note: Added to KEV 16 Jul 2026 — actively exploited

items.title: Gardyn IoT Hub flaws (CVSS 10) let attackers take over connected indoor-farming devices
items.content_text: CISA published ICSA-26-183-03 on 2 July for the Gardyn IoT Hub, an indoor/vertical-farming controller used in the US food and agriculture sector, assigning a maximum CVSS v3 base score of 10. The advisory covers hard-coded credentials, sensitive-information exposure and unsafe handling of HTTP header content in Gardyn Home and Studio firmware and the Gardyn Cloud API before v2.12.2026, which together could let an unauthenticated attacker access and control managed devices. It is consumer/small-scale precision-ag rather than a processing-plant controller, but it is a concrete example of how thinly-secured ag-IoT reaches the sector — and of the class of internet-connected grow/monitoring gear proliferating across agriculture.

items.title: Farm and food cybersecurity legislation advances with risk assessments and crisis drills
items.content_text: Food-sector cyber provisions keep advancing on Capitol Hill: the Farm and Food Cybersecurity Act would direct USDA, with CISA, to assess sector cyber threats every two years and run annual crisis-simulation exercises for food-related emergencies, and the Senate Agriculture Committee’s 2026 farm-bill discussion draft, released 15 July, carries cybersecurity investments for agricultural facilities into farm-bill priorities alongside the Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026. For operators the direction of travel is clear: periodic risk assessment and exercised incident response are becoming baseline expectations.
